subject: Renewal matrix: multi-wave term orchestration & staged-burst onramp
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@dataferry.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal matrix: multi-wave term orchestration & staged-burst onramp

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our product and finance sync I've put together a renewal matrix that is intended to give DataFerry flexibility while locking in predictable economics as you scale. High-level summary:

- Structure: 3-wave term (12mo base + 12mo ramp + optional 12mo extension) so you can stagger spend to match usage growth.
- Year 1: conservative committed baseline to cover steady production traffic.
- Year 2: pre-agreed ramp buckets with two burst credits windows to absorb onboarding and spike usage.
- Year 3: opt-in auto-renew EXCEPT for any explicit opt-out 60 days prior (we can flip to manual renewal if you prefer).
- Co-term: we can co-term DataFerry's three accounts onto the same renewal boundary with blended pricing on reserved capacity.

I've attached a matrix that shows pricing tiers, burst-credit mechanics, and example true-up timing (renewal_matrix_2028.xlsx). A few questions for you so we can finalize:

1) Do you want the ramp buckets to be invoiced monthly or quarterly?
2) Are there internal procurement constraints for the third-year auto-renew?
3) Would a short initial pilot (two-week free burst) to validate ramp assumptions be helpful?

If this looks reasonable, I'd like to schedule a 30-min alignment call with procurement + engineering next week to lock payment terms and the implementation cadence.

Thanks —

Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0189

Attachments: renewal_matrix_2028.xlsx (spreadsheet), DF-3921-multiwave-term-draft.pdf (PDF)

From: Samir Khan <samir@dataferry.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataFerry Procurement <procurement@dataferry.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Aug 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal matrix: multi-wave term orchestration & staged-burst onramp

Hi Camila —

Appreciate the clear layout. A few follow-ups from our side:

- Billing cadence: procurement prefers quarterly invoices for committed spend; is that compatible with your billing system?
- Burst credits: can unused burst credits roll forward into the next quarter in case we smooth spikes?
- Co-term mechanics: we have three separate legal entities (US, EU, APAC). Co-terming is OK for commercial alignment but procurement will need separate invoices per legal entity.
- Auto-renew opt-in: we would prefer auto-renew for pricing stability but would like a 30-day cancellation window rather than 60.

Also, any chance you can provide a provisional SOW-level milestone schedule tied to the Year-2 ramp (so engineering and our platform team can map integrations)?

Happy to do the 30-min call; availability next Thursday morning PST.

Best,
Samir Khan
Head of Platform Operations
DataFerry Inc.
samir@dataferry.com | +1 212-555-4490

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 09 Aug 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal matrix: multi-wave term orchestration & staged-burst onramp

Marissa / Karthik / Priyom —

Forwarding Samir's reply. Key asks: quarterly invoices per legal entity, roll-forward behavior for burst credits, shorten auto-renew cancellation window to 30 days, and a SOW-level Year-2 milestone schedule.

My recommendation (commercial concessions / ops):
- Accept quarterly invoicing with per-entity invoicing (no pricing change). Finance will need billing contacts for EU/APAC entities.
- Burst credits: propose "use-or-lose per quarter" by default, but offer a one-time rollover for up to 50% of unused credits in Q1 of Year-2 as a concession for onboarding risk.
- Auto-renew: move to 30-day cancellation window to keep the deal moving; if legal flags a problem we can revert to 60 days.
- SOW: Priyom / SE team to draft a lightweight milestone schedule (integration checkpoint, prefix caching enabled, QoS tests, post-onboarding review).

I think we can win this if we accept the quarterly invoicing and tighten the roll-forward to a controlled one-time rollover. The most likely blocker is procurement requesting separate PO process for each legal entity — need to know whether we can route invoices separately without losing the co-term pricing.

Suggested concession (if needed): one month of supplemental burst credits (equivalent to ~$12k) applied in the first ramp window. Approve?

- Camila

Subject: Re: Renewal matrix: multi-wave term orchestration & staged-burst onramp — next steps and call

Thanks Samir — this is helpful. Quick confirmation on next steps: 

1) Commercial: We can accommodate quarterly, per-entity invoices while preserving the co-term pricing. Finance will need billing contacts for each legal entity; sending separate invoice emails will be supported.

2) Burst credits: We will default to use-or-lose per quarter but are prepared to allow a one-time rollover of up to 50% of unused credits in the first Year-2 quarter to help with smoothing during integration.

3) Auto-renew: We can shorten the cancellation window to 30 days. Legal will add a line in the amendment that allows explicit monthly termination notice in the case of material breach.

4) SOW / Milestones: Priyom, could you draft a 6-line milestone schedule (integration kickoff, staging validation, prefix cache enablement, performance validation, production cutover, 30-day post-cutover review) and drop it into the Drive link by EOD Monday?

5) Concession: Approving one month of supplemental burst credits (~$12k value) to be applied to DataFerry's first ramp window — offered as an onboarding incentive and not recurring.

I've attached the updated term draft and a DocuSign link for the amendment (docusign-Df3921-term-amendment.link.txt). Let's lock the 30-min alignment call for Thu 16 Aug 9:30 AM PST — Samir, confirm and I'll send the calendar invite.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
